g.title: t_policy
g.text: groups: group:superuser plus one group per location
tags: tag:infra, tag:k8s, tag:k8s-operator, tag:k8s-recorder, tag:ci,
tag:ssh-granted, tag:lobby, per-location and per-person tags
ipsets: one per location (LAN /24 + service/pod/LB /16s), plus
autoApprovers: routes + exit nodes + Tailscale Services for tag:k8s
ssh: recorded sessions enforced through tag:k8s-recorder
grants: location-to-location only via that location's own subnet router,
cap/tsidp, and a custom cap/tsdnsproxy DNS-rewrite map
nodeAttrs: traffic-steering + app-connector domain sets, funnel for tag:k8s
tests + sshTests are committed alongside and run in CI

g.title: t_egress_contract
g.text: Pod-side tailnet contract — the rule that keeps breaking people
For every tailnet name a pod consumes, declare in the consuming namespace:
The operator rewrites externalName to a *.tailscale.svc.cluster.local proxy
and DNSConfig republishes the original .ts.net name as that proxy's ClusterIP.
Verify BOTH before wiring a client:
a throwaway pod resolves the .keiretsu.ts.net name
A laptop dig proves nothing — laptops use MagicDNS, pods do not.
Never publish tailnet CGNAT addresses (the 100.64/10 range) in public DNS.
Identity-authenticated protocols (Garage RPC) need one ingress identity and
one egress Service PER REMOTE NODE; a shared L4 VIP cannot route a node ID.
kro ResourceGraphDefinition serviceegress generates this pattern as a

g.title: t_proxyclass
g.text: common-dev common + a custom tun-service-metrics image (ingress default)
common-unstable common pinned to a tailscale unstable tag

g.title: t_csi
g.text: Secrets Store CSI provider + SecretProviderClass tailscale

g.title: t_syscompanion

g.title: t_examples

g.title: s_garage
g.text: GarageCluster garage — one per site, one logical S3 estate
remoteClusters lists ALL THREE zones, each reached over the tailnet:
GARAGE_STORAGE_LAYOUT_POLICY=Manual on all three: the storage tier is
hand-declared per node so an array can move between backing stores;
Apps never talk to the storage tier directly — they use
because the gateway carries the full FullReplication key_table (so S3
signature auth resolves locally) and survives local storage loss by
proxying reads to a surviving zone at read_quorum=1.

g.title: s_garage_op
g.text: ServiceMonitor + PrometheusRules enabled, admission webhooks on
two committed postRender patches, each with its reason:
metrics Service is relabelled app.kubernetes.io/component=metrics so the
ServiceMonitor stops 404-scraping the webhook Service on the same labels
the GarageNodeDisconnected rule is rewritten to
only when NO peer can see a node, not on self-observation

local-200 200Gi on orin-0 (tolerates the control-plane taint)
GARAGE_REPLICAS 2, pods pinned to instance-type dgx-spark

garage-webadmin/ at the repo root is the custom admin image, built by

g.title: s_ceph_ot

g.title: s_ceph_rb
g.text: ceph v20.2.2 · mon 3 with allowMultiplePerNode (only 3 machines)
mgr 2, rook module only · pod network, msgr2 NOT required
useAllDevices false — devices are listed explicitly per node:
stone nvme1n1 · titan nvme0n1, nvme1n1, sda, sdc, sdd
tank nvme* glob PLUS sdd named explicitly, because the glob that
excluded a destroyed disk was also hiding a healthy one
CephBlockPool ceph-blockpool-replicated-nvme size 3, host, deviceClass nvme
placement tolerates tuppr.home-operations.com/outdated: Rook rejects ANY
untolerated taint when validating OSD placement, so tuppr's
PreferNoSchedule taint silently stopped OSD creation on all three nodes
No CephObjectStore/RGW exists in either cluster — all object storage is Garage.

g.title: s_smb
g.text: STORAGECLASS_LONGTERM points here on both clusters

g.title: s_localpath
g.text: Storageclass for ALL THREE St. Petersburg tiers (default, metadata, longterm)

g.title: s_velero
g.text: Velero (chart 12.1.0, velero v1.18.2, aws plugin v1.14.2)
BackupStorageLocation garage — provider aws, bucket velero,
s3ForcePathStyle. The prefix MUST be a sibling of bucket; nested under
config it is silently ignored and every cluster shares one kopia repo.
volumeSnapshotLocation is empty — PV data is captured by kopia fs-backup
through the node agent, not by CSI snapshots
node-agent-config sets loadConcurrency 2 and prepareQueueLength 8, because
the default of 1 lets one wedged PodVolumeBackup fail the whole node
credentials come from a GarageKey-populated Secret, not the chart's file
velero-ui (Ottawa) exposes it; a bhaiya-velero Role lets the bhaiya
media-config deliberately sets defaultVolumesToFsBackup false — the bulk
data lives on Ceph/SMB and relies on storage-layer durability

g.title: s_cnpg
g.text: 10 Postgres Clusters, 2 instances each except lobby-postgres (1):
barman-cloud ObjectStore CRs push WAL and base backups to Garage at

Valkey — one genuine instance, searxng's local chart, storage disabled

g.title: s_zot
g.text: Zot OCI registry (chart 0.1.122, zot v2.1.20, Ottawa)
2 replicas, persistence FALSE — all state in Garage S3 plus Dragonfly
storageDriver s3, bucket zot, region garage, forcepathstyle
retention keeps the 10 most recently pushed and pulled tags, 720h windows
htpasswd auth from a SOPS-encrypted secret; anonymous read/create/update
sync extension mirrors ghcr.io on demand, 6h poll
search, UI and metrics extensions enabled

g.title: s_kafka
g.text: Strimzi / Kafka (Robbinsdale only — pointer is COMMENTED OUT)
Kafka robbinsdale, KRaft mode (no ZooKeeper), Kafka 4.3.0
listener raj :9092 cluster-ip, SCRAM-SHA-512 over TLS
4 TLSRoutes on the private Gateway (3 brokers + bootstrap)
The namespace directory and kustomization still list strimzi.yaml, but every

g.title: n_dns_public
g.text: DNS plane 1 — Cloudflare, for the PUBLIC tier
Consequence worth memorising: a ${CLUSTER_DOMAIN} route gets DNS for free the
moment it attaches to a gateway labelled gateway=public. A ${COMMON_DOMAIN}
name does NOT — it needs a hand-written DNSEndpoint entry, or it will report

g.title: n_dns_private
g.text: DNS plane 2 — UniFi, for the PRIVATE tier
sidecar image external-dns-unifi-webhook, UniFi API key SOPS-encrypted
sources crd + all four gateway route kinds + service
The dns-scope!=public-only filter exists because the UniFi static-DNS API
rejects wildcard hostnames with 400 Invalid Hostname, so the wildcard
DNSEndpoint is deliberately tagged out of this instance's view.

g.title: n_dns_ts
g.text: DNS plane 3 — Pi-hole, for the TAILNET tier
sources the four gateway route kinds
Pi-hole itself is reachable through the ts Gateway's :53 TCP and UDP

g.title: n_ddns
g.text: keeps ${LOCATION}.<domain> A/AAAA pointed at the site's current WAN address.
That record is the target every ExternalDNS CNAME and every k8gb pool

g.title: n_cnames
g.text: The two hand-written DNSEndpoints for keiretsu.top
proxied through Cloudflare: apex and www -> keiretsu.cdn.keiretsu.top
forgejo, velero, hubble, logs, prometheus, opencost, oci, status,
-> ottawa.keiretsu.top, i.e. straight to the Ottawa edge, bypassing GSLB:
auth, home, bhaiya, grafana, teslamate, litellm, woodpecker, infisical,
bhaiya is pinned here on purpose — through the GSLB the second WAN edge
Everything is cloudflare-proxied=false except the apex/www pair.

g.title: n_k8gb
g.text: k8gb — GSLB for the shared zone
negative TTL 30s, NS TTL 30s, requeue 60s, edge resolver is a public resolver
bundled CoreDNS: 3 replicas, priorityClass infra-high, LoadBalancer <LB>.10.53
Gateway API integration on; the extdns sidecar is off — the ExternalDNS
an extra CoreDNS template answers _acme-challenge.cdn.keiretsu.top so DNS-01
can still issue certificates for GSLB names
13 Gslb objects: keiretsu-web, dashboard-cdn, dashboard-ts-cdn, ts-gateway,
garage-s3-cdn, zot-public, forgejo, velero, prometheus, victoria-logs,
FAILOVER pairing from cluster-settings: ottawa<->robbinsdale, stpetersburg->ottawa
Two constraints learned the hard way:
a Gslb's HTTPRoute must name EXACTLY ONE parent Gateway, so CDN routes pin
an absent HTTPRoute reads as healthy, so an inert route is deployed to every
cluster to make per-cluster health actually drive pool membership

g.title: n_envoy
g.text: Envoy Gateway — three GatewayClasses per cluster
all three use controller gateway.envoyproxy.io/gatewayclass-controller with an
EnvoyProxy parameter object and a ClientTrafficPolicy of the same name
GatewayClass public -> Gateway public (ns home), LB <LB CIDR>.10.15
GatewayClass private -> Gateway private (ns home), LB <LB CIDR>.10.14
GatewayClass home-ts -> Gateway ts (ns home), published on the tailnet
The Gateways are defined ONCE in kubernetes/apps/base/home/home/ and reused
unmodified by all three clusters through ${CLUSTER_DOMAIN} / ${LOCATION}
substitution — there is no per-cluster Gateway overlay.
Lua extension policies are enabled on the controller, and the controller is
deliberately rolled after config changes because it does not always pick

g.title: n_gw_public
g.text: label gateway=public (what Cloudflare ExternalDNS filters on)
webrtc-tcp / webrtc-udp TCP/UDP :8555 Frigate live view, Ottawa only
The eighth listener looks wrong and is not. The hostname is parameterised per
cluster while the certificate reference is the literal name
wildcard-ottawa-keiretsu-top -- but that Secret is written by Certificate
wildcard-location-keiretsu-top, whose dnsNames ARE parameterised. So every
cluster stores its own *.<location>.keiretsu.top certificate under a name
that says ottawa: correct behaviour, misleading name. Repointing the
listener alone would aim it at a Secret that nothing writes.

g.title: n_gw_private
g.text: (the Strimzi TLSRoutes also target a kafka-listener on this tier)
Narrower than public on purpose: no hermes / bhaiya / cdn / s3 / location
sub-tiers and no WebRTC, because LAN traffic never needs them.
Not published to Cloudflare — it lacks the gateway=public label.

g.title: n_routes
g.text: private + ts the default for admin consoles: every *arr, sabnzbd,
the two qBittorrents, plex, prowlarr, garage-webui,
cluster, victoria-logs, rook dashboard, goldpinger, k9s
public as well overseerr, tautulli, wizarr, plex, and the Ottawa-only
public only the CDN tier — every route in namespace keiretsu-top,
generated from the components/cdn-site template, which
rewrites the Host header and sends traffic to garage-gateway
three Homers dashboard-private, dashboard-public and dashboard-ts are three
separate deployments sharing the hostname home.${CLUSTER_DOMAIN},
one per tier; the homepage app additionally serves
three tiers and 301 grafana.<cluster domain> to the canonical
kro approute a ResourceGraphDefinition that generates Homer-annotated
HTTPRoutes from a short schema, for self-service exposure
Per-cluster divergences: Frigate is WAN-reachable only from Ottawa (it owns
the WebRTC routes); the Rook dashboard is ts-only on Ottawa but private+ts on
Robbinsdale; Plex adds the ts tier only on Robbinsdale; Home Assistant's
overlays drop the public tier the base template offers.

g.title: n_auth
g.text: tinyauth-killinit serves auth.killinit.cc — suwayomi needs a cookie scoped
to killinit.cc, not the shared keiretsu.top one
tinyauth-ts a Tailscale Service in front of the same pods
tinyauth-egress Robbinsdale and St. Petersburg run no local Tinyauth; a
headless Service plus pinned Endpoints reaches the Ottawa
Tinyauth only AUTHENTICATES (Google) and injects Remote-User, Remote-Email,
Remote-Name and Remote-Groups. Every protected route then carries its own
Envoy Gateway SecurityPolicy with extAuth pointing at the tinyauth Service
and an authorization block that is defaultAction Deny plus an explicit
Remote-Email allow-list. There is no central role model — access is
per-route, per-person, and visible in the manifest.
ReferenceGrant extauth-to-tinyauth admits SecurityPolicies from home,
bhaiya, keiretsu-top, velero-system, teslamate, monz, cliproxy and media.
An EnvoyExtensionPolicy carries a few lines of Lua that turn Tinyauth's 401
(which carries an x-tinyauth-location header) into a 302 so browsers follow
the login flow. It is duplicated on homepage, cliproxy, frigate and grafana-cdn.
kromgo is intentionally unauthenticated on the public tier -- it serves only
the badge endpoints this README renders. Tailnet-only routes rely on tailnet

g.title: n_cloudflared
g.text: an outbound-only Cloudflare tunnel, so Robbinsdale can publish without an
inbound port forward — an ingress path that bypasses its Envoy public tier

g.title: o_kps
g.text: delivered from an OCIRepository, not a HelmRepository
prometheus externalLabels cluster=${CLUSTER_NAME} — this is what keeps the
three clusters' series apart once they land in one Mimir
alertmanager enabled, with a SOPS-encrypted config secret and an
node-exporter and kube-state-metrics on; the bundled Grafana is DISABLED
because Grafana is a single Ottawa deployment
a committed patch fights the chart's honorTimestamps=true on the cadvisor

g.title: o_mimir
g.text: Mimir — the long-term metric store, Ottawa only
blocks + ruler on Garage S3, bucket mimir (ruler under prefix ruler/)
gateway (nginx) 2 replicas so remote-write survives a rollout
reachable on the tailnet as mimir.keiretsu.ts.net:8080 and
Robbinsdale and St. Petersburg deploy only mimir-egress — the ExternalName
Services that make the local mimir-gateway name resolve to Ottawa

g.title: o_vl
g.text: VictoriaLogs — the log store, Ottawa only
published as victoria-logs.keiretsu.ts.net plus a ts-gateway route
The trick worth copying: VICTORIA_LOGS_HOST is the SAME string in all three
that name is the real Service. In the other two clusters the location tree
ships only an ExternalName Service of exactly that name pointing at the
tailnet FQDN, so Fluent Bit needs no per-cluster configuration at all.

g.title: o_fb
g.text: a tcp listener on 5170 that receives Talos KERNEL logs, because
outputs two loki-protocol outputs to ${VICTORIA_LOGS_HOST}:9428, gzip,
VL-Msg-Field log for kube.* and msg for talos.*

g.title: o_grafana
g.text: grafana-operator based: app + instance + dashboards + datasources
mimir-gateway; the cluster label separates them), VictoriaLogs,
grafana-mcp exposes Grafana to agents over MCP
Robbinsdale and St. Petersburg deploy grafana-redirect /
grafana-redirect-stpetersburg instead of a second Grafana, so
grafana.<their domain> lands on the Ottawa instance

g.title: o_monz
g.text: its own VictoriaLogs and VictoriaMetrics HelmReleases, Grafana instance,
datasources and dashboard, published at monz.keiretsu.top with its own
ts ingress routes for the VL and VM components
kept deliberately separate from the primary monitoring namespace

g.title: o_gatus
g.text: published at status.<cluster domain>, and status.keiretsu.top via GSLB
probes both in-cluster endpoints and their tailnet equivalents — for
mimir.keiretsu.ts.net:8080/ready, so a mesh break is distinguishable

g.title: o_kromgo
g.text: serves cluster_* badge endpoints at kromgo.<cluster domain>
runs an nginx mimir-proxy sidecar and points KROMGO_PROMETHEUS_URL at
127.0.0.1:9090/prometheus, so the badges read from Mimir
exposed on the public Gateway — this is what renders the shields at the

g.title: o_probes
g.text: Probes: app-k8s-api-readyz (http_401 against the API readyz),
PrometheusRule blackbox-exporter.rules alerts on 5m failure and >5s latency
smartctl-exporter disk health, Ottawa and Robbinsdale (they have the disks)
unpoller UniFi controller metrics, all three clusters
k8gb-prometheus / k8gb-monitoring / k8gb-dashboard GSLB visibility, Ottawa
hubble-ui Cilium flow visibility, all three clusters
flux-monitoring Flux controller ServiceMonitors and dashboards

g.title: k_media_ot
g.text: media-apps — Ottawa (Flux Kustomization media-apps, ns media)
plex · overseerr · tautulli · wizarr · maintainerr · kometa
sabnzbd · qb · qb-pvt (usenet + two torrent clients)
lidarr · audiobookshelf · komga · suwayomi · bookorbit · shelfmark
Ottawa-only titles: audiobookshelf, komga, suwayomi, bookorbit,
bulk libraries live on the nagato-smb share; databases on Ceph RBD
qBittorrent is private+ts only. Its public CDN route was removed: the
pod-CIDR auth whitelist made Envoy traffic bypass qBittorrent login

g.title: k_media_rb
g.text: the same stack minus the book/manga/audiobook titles:
plex · overseerr · tautulli · wizarr · maintainerr · kometa
bulk libraries on the unas-smb share; databases on ceph-block-replicated-nvme

g.title: k_home
g.text: home namespace — the shared portal (all three clusters)
homer second dashboard, generated by homer-operator
dnsrecords DNSEndpoint objects for site-local names
local-gateway the public and private Gateways, GatewayClasses, EnvoyProxies
tailscale-gateway the ts Gateway, its GatewayClass and EnvoyProxy
St. Petersburg runs home-assistant as its own namespace instead

g.title: k_ai
g.text: ai namespace — inference on the DGX Sparks (St. Petersburg)
leader pinned to spark-0, worker on spark-1
vLLM serving DeepSeek V4 Flash, NVFP4 quantized
BOTH machines and the two halves talk over the 192.168.74.0/30 RDMA rail
(VLLM_HOST_IP / MASTER_ADDR are the RDMA addresses, not the LAN ones)
separate head and worker model PVCs; a drop-caches loop keeps page cache
Deployment vllm — replicas 0, a standby Qwen3.6-27B image with modelopt
quantization, 200k context and dflash speculative decoding
HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN comes from a SOPS-encrypted secret
Consumers reach it as stpetersburg-vllm.keiretsu.ts.net — hermes and
cliproxy both declare that egress Service.

g.title: k_gpu
g.text: driver and toolkit DISABLED — Talos extensions provide both
runtimeClass nvidia, device-plugin 1 replica per GPU (no time-slicing:
a single vLLM consumer gains nothing from fake slots)
mig.strategy none — GB10 has no MIG firmware path
gfd on, dcgm-exporter on with a ServiceMonitor
validator runs with WITH_WORKLOAD=false — there is no spare GPU to test on
nfd disabled here, which is why the GPU labels are hand-set in node patches
rdma-shared-dp exposes the spark-to-spark RDMA devices to pods
lws-system the LeaderWorkerSet controller dsv4 depends on
(Ottawa). kata-tailscale is the only one with the Talos
PodSecurity exemption, which is what lets an embedded
Tailscale workspace open a TUN device.
A kata-canary Deployment health-checks the runtime.
gvisor the other sandbox RuntimeClass, all three clusters
agent-sandbox the sandbox controller, all three clusters

g.title: k_ottawa_apps
g.text: bhaiya workspace/sandbox control plane. Reconciled from its OWN
GitRepository (Forgejo) via a Flux Receiver, not from this repo.
cert-manager, buzz. Owns a Velero Role so it can back itself up,
plus gateway RBAC and a *.bhaiya.keiretsu.top wildcard.
hermes agent runtime (hermes-agent); egresses to stpetersburg-vllm
buzz app + infra split: Postgres, Dragonfly, MinIO-compatible bits
firecrawl web-scraping stack, reconciled straight from the upstream
cliproxy LLM API proxy (cli-proxy-api); egress to stpetersburg-vllm
forgejo self-hosted Git — and the source of truth for bhaiya.
SSH on :22 through the private and ts Gateways.
woodpecker CI paired with Forgejo, with a persistent Nix cache workspace
searxng metasearch, backed by the one real Valkey in the repo
teslamate vehicle telemetry + a secret-sync helper and a Grafana datasource
immich photos (also on Robbinsdale); vectorchord Postgres + Dragonfly
zot OCI registry, plus zot-cache-ottawa for the shared Dragonfly
lan ExternalName entries for LAN appliances
tempvm on-demand VM gateway, published as a Tailscale Service
headlamp Kubernetes UI · opencost cost attribution
grafana-mcp MCP bridge in front of Grafana

All three actions-runner-controller + runner scale sets that dial out to
GitHub, spegel peer-to-peer image mirroring, default-debug and

g.title: k_platform
g.text: infra-default 500000000 everything else that must not
memory-request-floor raises implausibly small memory requests
kro ResourceGraphDefinitions turn repeated shapes into one
spegel nodes serve image layers to each other; this is why
tuppr drives Talos and Kubernetes upgrades, gated on Node
open-cluster-management Ottawa is the hub (ocm + ocm-grpc-lb); every cluster

g.title: sp_ext
g.text: driver choice NONFREE, not open-kernel-modules: the open modules crashed
the GB10 on boot and the rollback was done over UEFI. The
spark schematic also bakes in the arm64.nobti workaround.
kernel args apparmor=0, mitigations=off, security=none, auditd disabled,
net.ifnames=0 (five NICs can reorder, so NICs are pinned
spark modules nvidia, nvidia_uvm, nvidia_drm, nvidia_modeset + RDMA stack
sysctls BBR base + bpf_jit_enable=1 for Cilium,
vm.min_free_kbytes 4 GiB for multi-GiB weight loads
evictionHard memory.available 6Gi — added after spark-0 was
wedged twice by a 74 GB weight load with no reservations
containerd per-node, default_runtime_name=nvidia on the sparks only
GPU labels set by hand in node patches (Talos has no in-band NFD):

g.title: ot_ext
g.text: control-plane extensions amd-ucode, amdgpu, gvisor, kata-containers,
shiro extensions gvisor, i915, intel-ucode, kata-containers,
sysctls BBR + fq qdisc, 64 MiB socket buffers, TCP fastopen,
containerd CDI spec dirs, unprivileged ports/icmp,
discard_unpacked_layers=false so Spegel can serve layers
PodSecurity admission exemption for RuntimeClass kata-tailscale

g.title: rb_titan
g.text: moved off SFP after a multicast storm; the static
address is what keeps the Ceph mons stable
most disks of the three nodes

g.title: rb_ext
g.text: extensions amd-ucode, amdgpu, gvisor, i915, intel-ucode,
(mixed AMD+Intel set for mixed hardware in one node group)
kernel args talos.platform=metal only — no perf/mitigation tuning here
sysctls same BBR / inotify / hugepages / userns base as Ottawa
no per-node patch directory exists for this cluster

g.title: sp_orin
g.text: orin-0 · sole control plane · holds VIP 192.168.73.25
NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super dev kit
onboard M.2 NVMe for the OS (the SD card is unused)
Tegra iGPU present but deliberately unused —
no NVIDIA kernel modules loaded, minimal Talos schematic
8 GiB RAM, so no hugepage reservation
